items.question: What are the main parts of a web application such as an online shopping site?
items.answer: Answer: A web application has three parts. The front end is the part that you see and use in the browser. The back end is the software in the middle that receives the requests from the front end, talks to the database and sends back the result. The database is where the information (for example, the products of the shopping site) is stored. Building all three parts is called full stack development.

items.question: What is the front end, and which technologies are used to build it?
items.answer: Answer: The front end is the part of the application that the user sees and interacts with, for example the page that opens when you type the address of a shopping site, with its list of laptops. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and a tool such as React is used to make it more interactive. HTML builds the skeleton (the structure) of the page. CSS adds the colours and styling on top of the skeleton, like colours and clothes on a body. JavaScript gives the page the power to interact with the user, for example reacting when the user clicks. The front end should be interactive, because if the user cannot interact with it, nobody will use the application.

items.question: What happens when you click on a product, for example a laptop, on a shopping site?
items.answer: Answer: The details of the laptop are not in the front end. When you click, the front end sends a request to the back end. The back end goes to the database, fetches the information of that product, and returns it to the front end, and the front end displays the details on the screen. So the flow is: click in the front end, request to the back end, back end fetches from the database, response to the front end, and the details are displayed.

items.question: What is a database, and what is a DBMS?
items.answer: Answer: A database is the place where the information of the application is stored, for example the products, their prices and details. It is managed by software called a DBMS (Database Management System). There are many DBMS software, and SQL is the language used to work with them.

items.question: What is the back end, and why is it needed between the front end and the database?
items.answer: Answer: The back end is the middle layer of the application. The front end is not powerful enough to go to the database by itself and fetch the information. A powerful middle layer is needed: the back end takes the request of the front end, gets the data from the database and hands it back to the front end, which renders (displays) it. The back end can be built with many technologies, such as Java, Python, Go or Rust. In this course, Python is used.

items.question: What happens when you type a website address, such as instagram.com, in the browser?
items.answer: Answer: Your browser sends a request over the internet to a data center. A data center has powerful computers (servers) that handle many things internally and prepare the response. The response then comes back from the data center to your computer, and the browser shows the page. Building such requests (URLs) and responding to them is a part of back end development.

items.question: What is full stack development?
items.answer: Answer: Full stack development means developing all the parts of an application: the front end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React), the back end (for example Python with its frameworks) and the database (with SQL). A person who knows all of them can build a complete application.

items.question: What rounds can you expect in a company's interview process?
items.answer: Answer: The process is described as three rounds. Round 1 is a coding round (about 95 percent of the companies now have coding in the first round instead of aptitude, although aptitude still exists in some). Round 2 is the technical round, usually face to face. Round 3 is the HR round, where the interviewer checks your mindset, your behaviour and how you will contribute to the team, for example with the question "introduce yourself" and scenario-based questions. Clearing all three rounds is required to get the job.

items.question: What kind of questions are asked in the coding round and the technical round?
items.answer: Answer: Coding round: problems on strings (for example finding the sub-strings of a string), arrays (for example the second largest element in an array), and concepts such as the greedy approach, sliding window and linked lists. Technical round: concept questions, such as the difference between a set and a dictionary, the internal data structure of a dictionary (a hash table), and questions on generators, decorators and special methods in Python. You must understand the concept, not only memorise the answer.
